name: interpolate
what: writes a SECOND file at 2, 3 or 4 times the frame rate, with frames created between the originals (RIFE). The faithful file is delivered as always; in the copy the original frames are unchanged and the rest is invented
when: ONLY when the person asks for smoother motion or for the missing frames of a low-frame-rate source. Set the recipe's `interpolate` (2, 3 or 4), never as a step. Say plainly how many frames are created
softens: created frames morph fast movement instead of drawing it, and repeat ghosting when a source frame is itself a blend; no check can vouch for them
tried_on: owner cartoon at 10 fps, x3 on a 12 s cut: slow movement convincing, fast movement morphed, a ghosted source frame spread into its neighbours. The anime RIFE model did not run; the general one did
